2026-05-09T18:51:01.9838801Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9839149Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9839438Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9849406Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9850234Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9850729Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9852243Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9853903Z >
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9854632Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9855371Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9855547Z ### How to Use
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9855762Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9856249Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9856914Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9857066Z ```bash
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9857419Z # Discover what tools a server provides
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9857923Z <server-name> --help
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9858156Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9858508Z # Get detailed help for a specific tool (type, required status, description)
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9859167Z <server-name> <tool-name> --help
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9859460Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9859751Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9860783Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9862515Z ```
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9862711Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9862972Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9863442Z ```bash
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9863922Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9864643Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9865427Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9866971Z ```
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9867160Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9867484Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs):
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9868819Z ```bash
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9869337Z safeoutputs --help                                 # list all safe-output tools
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9870715Z safeoutputs add_comment --help                     # show types and required params
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9871562Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9872190Z ```
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9872365Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9872676Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9873196Z ```bash
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9873648Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9874463Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9875087Z ```
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9875913Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9876155Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9876544Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9877888Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9879608Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9879753Z ```bash
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9880379Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9881155Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9881927Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9882203Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9882666Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9883709Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9884449Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9884854Z ```
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9885028Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9885735Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9886590Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9886741Z ```bash
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9887343Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9888162Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9888807Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9889215Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9889583Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9970967Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9971596Z ```
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9971787Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9971973Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9972819Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9974766Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9975692Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9976609Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9977499Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9977971Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9978120Z ### Notes
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9978322Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9978907Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9980507Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9981663Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9983597Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9984748Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9985823Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9986713Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9987331Z </mcp-clis>

2026-05-09T18:51:02.0003535Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0003688Z ## Workflow
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0003894Z

2026-05-09T18:51:02.0006303Z    - Use it to avoid repositories that have already been tested unless the manual input explicitly asks for a rerun.

2026-05-09T18:51:02.0026223Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0026685Z    - Select up to `MAX_REPOS` repositories. Prefer a small, diverse set over a huge one. Default to 5.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0027999Z    - If the default pool is exhausted, pick other well-known public repositories with distinct ecosystems and conventional config files.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0028811Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0028974Z 3. Prepare and run.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0029435Z    - Call `real_world_prepare_corpus` with `clone: true`.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0031067Z    - If it reports duplicates, choose replacements unless this was an intentional manual rerun.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0032692Z    - Call `real_world_run_corpus` with the prepared `corpusDir`, `cacheDir`, and `outputArtifact`.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0035088Z    - Nonzero validation exit code 1 is expected when real issues are found. Treat crashes, missing output JSON, hangs, and unexplained warnings as higher-severity product signals.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0036917Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0037096Z 4. Triage the output.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0037582Z    - Inspect the DollarLint JSON output artifact with `jq`.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0038631Z    - Separate parsing, validation, schema, coverage, warnings, crashes, performance, and output-contract findings.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0040510Z    - Decide whether each finding is a real third-party issue, expected test fixture data, SchemaStore mismatch, parser compatibility gap, confusing output/reporting problem, or DollarLint bug.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0042871Z    - Summarize product recommendations before finishing the run. Each recommendation must include a strength label of `high`, `med`, or `low`, based on frequency, severity, reproducibility, and expected user impact.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0044095Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0045628Z 5. Persist repository memory.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0048991Z    - Call `real_world_record_result` with the title, corpus, cache directory, command, output artifact, repositories, findings, product recommendations with strength labels in `productDecisions`, and follow-up notes.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0051970Z    - Also append a factual narrative entry to `reports/REAL-WORLD-TESTS.md` using the existing report shape.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0054380Z    - If files changed, request a pull request through the configured `create-pull-request` safe output. Keep the PR title concise and mention the structured result file.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0056489Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0057535Z 6. Publish the report.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0062101Z    - Request one GitHub Discussion through the configured `create-discussion` safe output.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0063174Z    - Title: use the run date and a short result summary, for example `2026-05-09 - 5 repo corpus`.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0066772Z    - Body style:
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0067210Z      - Use `###` and `####` headings only.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0068223Z      - Keep the summary, result counts, notable findings, and product recommendations with `high`/`med`/`low` strength labels visible.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0069460Z      - Put verbose per-file details and raw warnings inside `<details>` blocks.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0070659Z      - Include the tested repository table, DollarLint commit, output artifact path, and workflow run URL.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0078288Z    - If Discussion creation is unavailable, the safe output may fall back to an issue; mention that the intended destination was a Discussion.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0080111Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0081065Z Do not fabricate results. If cloning or validation fails before a meaningful corpus run, publish a short failure report with the blocker, partial artifacts, and the next concrete fix.
